reasons.plausibility: The hypothesis is scientifically sound in principle, but it lacks specific evidence from prior elemental or binary results and does not address how the ML potential will be trained on free-energy data (which requires the very costly calculations it aims to replace), creating a circular dependency.
reasons.testability: The proposed test is clear and decisive, with well-defined quantitative falsification criteria, but it is limited to elemental and binary systems and does not address the core challenge of multicomponent high-entropy systems stated in the research question.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis is moderately useful as it proposes a common ML-surrogate approach, but it fails to provide a novel methodological intervention to substantially reduce cost for high-entropy systems, which is the central constraint of the question.
